# mcloud db

<!-- Generated by `go run ./internal/gendocs`: edit the source it names, not this file. -->

_Generated from the command's help in `internal/cli`._

[All commands](README.md)

An app's database: migrate it, restore it, recover it, branch it.

For apps whose database the maxcloud controller runs (db: in
maxcloud.yaml, or mcloud apps set &lt;app&gt; --db). Its backups are
generations: db-1, db-2, ... in the bucket mc-&lt;app&gt;--db; every restore
starts a new one and leaves the older ones as they are.

| Command | |
| --- | --- |
| [`mcloud db branch`](#mcloud-db-branch) | Throwaway copies of the database, now or at a point in time |
| [`mcloud db migrate`](#mcloud-db-migrate) | Apply the app's SQL migrations (migrations/\*.sql) to its database |
| [`mcloud db proxy`](#mcloud-db-proxy) | Reach the app's database (or a branch's) on localhost |
| [`mcloud db psql`](#mcloud-db-psql) | Open psql in the app's database (or a branch's) |
| [`mcloud db recover`](#mcloud-db-recover) | Unblock a Blocked database by picking the backup generation to restore |
| [`mcloud db restore`](#mcloud-db-restore) | Restore the database, in place, to how it was at a point in time |

## mcloud db branch

Throwaway copies of the database, now or at a point in time.

A branch is the app's database restored from its backups into a
Postgres of its own (Cluster db-&lt;name&gt;; its URL is in the Secret
db-&lt;name&gt;-app, key uri). It doesn't back itself up and changes nothing in
the database: for trying a migration, a preview deploy, or looking at the
data as it was. It counts against the app's quota until you delete it.

| Command | |
| --- | --- |
| [`mcloud db branch create`](#mcloud-db-branch-create) | Branch the database |
| [`mcloud db branch delete`](#mcloud-db-branch-delete) | Delete a branch and its Postgres |
| [`mcloud db branch list`](#mcloud-db-branch-list) | List the database's branches |

## mcloud db branch create

Branch the database.

```
mcloud db branch create [APP] NAME [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud db branch create shop try-migration
mcloud db branch create shop yesterday --at 24h
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--at` string |  | the point in time (default: the latest) |
| `--wait` | `true` | wait until the branch is ready |

## mcloud db branch delete

Delete a branch and its Postgres.

```
mcloud db branch delete [APP] NAME
```

## mcloud db branch list

List the database's branches.

```
mcloud db branch list [APP]
```

## mcloud db migrate

Apply the app's SQL migrations (migrations/\*.sql) to its database.

Apply the files in migrations/ (in the app's folder: source: in
maxcloud.yaml, else next to it; or --dir) that the
database hasn't had yet, in name order, each in its own transaction. Name
them NUMBER\_DESCRIPTION.sql with numbers of one width: 0001\_init.sql,
0002\_add\_orders.sql. The database records each one it applied, with a
checksum, in the table maxcloud\_migrations; a file edited after it was
applied stops the run. Only one run applies at a time.

It reaches the deployed app's database (or a branch's) through a
port-forward, as the app's own user, and asks before it changes the app's
database. --database-url applies them to any Postgres instead.

Apps on the SDKs don't need this to deploy: they apply their pending
migrations themselves when they start. mcloud dev applies them to the
database it runs the app with.

```
mcloud db migrate [APP] [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud db migrate --dry-run
mcloud db migrate
mcloud db migrate shop --branch try-migration
mcloud db migrate --database-url postgres://postgres:dev@127.0.0.1:5432/app
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--branch` string |  | a branch of the database (mcloud db branch list) |
| `--database-url` string |  | apply to this Postgres instead of the app's database |
| `--dir` string |  | the migrations directory (default: migrations/ in the app's folder, source: or next to maxcloud.yaml) |
| `--dry-run` |  | list the applied and pending migrations, apply none |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  | don't ask |

## mcloud db proxy

Reach the app's database (or a branch's) on localhost.

Forward a local port to the database's primary and print a DATABASE\_URL
for it, as the app's own user, until you stop it (Ctrl-C). For a GUI, a
migration tool, or running the app locally (mcloud dev --db branch:NAME
does that by itself).

```
mcloud db proxy [APP] [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud db proxy
mcloud db proxy shop --branch try-migration --port 5433
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--branch` string |  | a branch of the database (mcloud db branch list) |
| `--port` int |  | local port (default: any free one) |

## mcloud db psql

Open psql in the app's database (or a branch's).

Run psql in the database's primary, as the postgres superuser, in the app
database. Interactive on a terminal; otherwise it runs what comes on
stdin.

```
mcloud db psql [APP] [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud db psql
mcloud db psql shop --branch try-migration
echo 'select count(*) from maxcloud_jobs' | mcloud db psql
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--branch` string |  | a branch of the database (mcloud db branch list) |

## mcloud db recover

Unblock a Blocked database by picking the backup generation to restore.

The controller stops (Blocked) instead of guessing when it can't account
for what's in the backup bucket. Look at the generations (the folders db-N
in mc-&lt;app&gt;--db), pick one, and it restores that one into a new
generation.

```
mcloud db recover [APP] --from GENERATION [flags]
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--from` int |  | the backup generation to restore (required) |

## mcloud db restore

Restore the database, in place, to how it was at a point in time.

Takes the database down and brings it back as it was at TIME, from its
backups. Everything written after TIME is gone from the database; it stays
in the older generation's backups for as long as they're kept.

TIME is RFC 3339 (2026-11-05T10:00:00Z), a local date and time
(2026-11-05 10:00), or how long ago (15m, 2h).

To try a point in time without touching the database, branch it instead:
mcloud db branch create &lt;name&gt; --at TIME.

```
mcloud db restore [APP] --at TIME [flags]
```

Examples:

```fish
mcloud db restore shop --at 15m
mcloud db restore shop --at "2026-11-05 10:00"
```

Flags:

| Flag | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--at` string |  | the point in time (required) |
| `--wait` | `true` | wait until the database is back |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  | don't ask |
